answer: Cohort-split inspection: each ID is stamped with its registration week, and an answer settles only when 4 graders from at least 3 other weeks pass it; grades from the author's own cohort count zero. Farms are minted in bursts, so 1,000 clones grown off one vine share a cohort and can't sign off each other's work, like a framer barred from inspecting his own walls. To self-pass, a farm must keep IDs alive across 3+ separate weeks and still outvote honest graders in each, a thin ledge. One thread of shared birth date sinks them. Proposed rule, not measured.
